# vue-rtl-kit — full documentation reference

> vue-rtl-kit is an MIT-licensed Vue 3.3+ and Nuxt 3/4 toolkit for reactive direction state, local RTL/LTR scopes, logical styles, locale-aware formatting, and simplified plain-text bidirectional isolation. This reference summarizes the documented API and links to each English and Arabic guide.

Documentation: https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/
Arabic documentation: https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/
Source: https://github.com/MarwanMaher0/vue-rtl-kit

## Installation and support

Vue 3.3 or later and Node 20.11+ are required. The Nuxt module supports Nuxt 3 and 4; Nuxt provides the optional @nuxt/kit peer. The package has no runtime dependencies beyond Vue. The optional stylesheet is exported separately.

Install from npm:

```sh
npm install vue-rtl-kit
```

This toolkit is not a message-translation library, a rich-text engine, an automatic interface converter, or a complete implementation of the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. Keep your translation library and use native CSS logical properties for ordinary layouts. Use BidiText only for plain-text run isolation and test the actual scripts and strings your application displays.

Sources:
- [Getting started](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/getting-started)
- [ابدأ الآن](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/getting-started)

## Vue setup

Create an app-level store once and install that same object as the Vue plugin:

```ts
import { createApp } from 'vue'
import { createRtl } from 'vue-rtl-kit'
import 'vue-rtl-kit/styles.css'
import App from './App.vue'

const rtl = createRtl({
  locales: { en: 'ltr', ar: 'rtl' },
  defaultLocale: 'ar',
})

createApp(App).use(rtl).mount('#app')
```

By default, installation registers BidiText, RtlProvider, and v-rtl globally, exposes $rtl for Options API components, and synchronizes the browser document's dir and lang attributes. The CSS import is optional in plain Vue. Retain the store reference for application setup, router guards, or other code outside components.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDirection } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

const { isRtl, setLocale } = useDirection()
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="setLocale(isRtl ? 'en' : 'ar')">
    {{ isRtl ? 'English' : 'العربية' }}
  </button>
  <BidiText as="p" text="الإصدار v1.2.3 متاح الآن" />
</template>
```

Use setLocale() for language-driven direction. Use setDirection() or toggleDirection() only when direction is an independent choice that should remain pinned.

## createRtl options

Signature: `createRtl(options?: RtlOptions): RtlInstance`.

- locales: string[] or Record<string, 'rtl' | 'ltr'>; default {}. An array infers directions; a map specifies them explicitly.
- defaultLocale: initial language, defaulting to the first locale key or 'en'.
- dir: optional explicit initial direction. Supplying it pins direction rather than allowing later locale changes to drive it.
- syncDocument: true by default. Keeps browser html dir and lang synchronized.
- htmlClass: false by default. true toggles rtl/ltr classes; an object such as { rtl: 'is-rtl', ltr: 'is-ltr' } supplies custom class names.
- numberingSystem: optional string or per-locale map for useFormat, such as { ar: 'latn' }.
- registerGlobals: true by default. false avoids global component/directive registration in plain Vue; import components and vRtl explicitly instead.
- persist: false by default; 'localStorage' or 'cookie' saves the locale in the browser on every setLocale() and restores it on the next createRtl(). Browser-only: nothing is read or written at import time or on the server. A stored value is restored only when it is a configured locale (a tag in locales or one whose language subtag is listed); with no locales, any tag Intl.getCanonicalLocales accepts, restored in its canonical spelling. Unknown values fall back to defaultLocale, a pinned dir option stays pinned, and storage errors are silently ignored. The cookie is written with path=/, SameSite=Lax, a one-year max-age, and an encoded name and value. dispose() stops the writes.
- persistKey: 'rtl-locale' by default; the localStorage item name or cookie name used by persist. The Nuxt module excludes persist and persistKey from ModuleOptions and persists through its SSR-aware cookie option instead.

The returned root instance exposes resolved options, install(app), and dispose(). dispose() stops document synchronization and persistence writes; it does not undo Vue provides or unregister components.

Sources:
- [createRtl](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/create-rtl)
- [إعداد createRtl](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/create-rtl)

## Direction state, locale resolution, and pinning

DirectionContext contains reactive dir and locale refs; computed isRtl/isLtr, startSide/endSide, and sign; setDirection, toggleDirection, setLocale, htmlAttrs; and an isRoot flag. sign is 1 in LTR and -1 in RTL. startSide is left in LTR and right in RTL.

Direction follows locale until pinned. An explicit initial dir, setDirection(), or toggleDirection() pins the root direction. Later setLocale() calls change the locale but do not recalculate that pinned direction. There is no documented public unpin action on RtlInstance. Omit dir and use setLocale() alone for language-driven switching.

```ts
import { createRtl } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

const rtl = createRtl({ locales: ['en', 'ar', 'he'], defaultLocale: 'en' })
rtl.setLocale('ar')
rtl.setDirection('ltr')
rtl.setLocale('he')
```

After the first setLocale, direction is RTL. After the explicit setDirection, it is pinned LTR and remains LTR when the locale changes to Hebrew.

Locale helpers include directionOfLocale(locale, fallback?), normaliseLocales(locales), resolveDirection(locale, locales, fallback?), oppositeDirection(dir), and RTL_LANGUAGES. Resolution supports exact locale maps, language subtags, and script-based inference: az-Arab is RTL, ku-Latn is LTR, and ar-EG can use the ar map entry.

For standalone state, createDirectionState({ dir, locale, locales?, pinned? }) returns the same reactive state/actions without isRoot, options, install, dispose, or document synchronization.

SSR never touches the DOM. In a manual Vue SSR shell, rtl.htmlAttrs() returns the actual { dir, lang } for the document. Create request-appropriate state rather than sharing a mutable app instance across users. Nuxt handles its document integration through the module.

Sources:
- [Direction store](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/direction-store)
- [مخزن الاتجاه](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/direction-store)

## useDirection and useRtl

useDirection(): DirectionContext reads the nearest RtlProvider scope, then the installed app-level root, then a shared detached LTR/en fallback. It does not throw when the plugin is absent. The detached fallback does not synchronize the document. Inside a provider, its setters affect that local scope rather than the application root.

useRtl(): RtlInstance always accesses the installed app-level root, even inside a provider. It throws if createRtl was not installed. Use it for a global language control embedded in a locally directed panel. Its return value includes options, install, and dispose in addition to DirectionContext.

Vue templates unwrap destructured refs. In script, access dir.value, locale.value, and other refs explicitly.

```ts
import { useDirection, useRtl } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

const { dir, locale, setLocale } = useDirection()
const root = useRtl()
```

Sources:
- [useDirection](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/use-direction)
- [useDirection بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/use-direction)
- [useRtl](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/use-rtl)
- [useRtl بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/use-rtl)

## RtlProvider: local layout islands

RtlProvider gives a subtree its own direction, locale, DOM attributes, and reactive context without changing the root store.

Props:
- dir: optional rtl/ltr. Without it, direction comes from the locale prop or the parent.
- locale: optional language, otherwise inherited from the parent; sets lang.
- tag: wrapper tag, default 'div'. null renders only slot content.
- isolate: true by default; applies unicode-bidi: isolate on the wrapper.

The wrapper receives dir, lang, and data-rtl-scope. The slot exposes dir, isRtl, setDirection, and toggleDirection. useDirection(), useLogicalStyles(), useFormat(), and BidiText inside the provider use that scope. External dir and locale prop changes remain authoritative; without either prop, the provider follows its parent direction.

```vue
<RtlProvider dir="ltr" tag="pre">
  <code>git checkout -b feature/rtl</code>
</RtlProvider>
```

A renderless provider (`:tag="null"`) provides reactive context but creates no DOM element to carry direction. Put direction attributes on its children when DOM direction or isolation matters.

Sources:
- [RtlProvider](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/rtl-provider)
- [RtlProvider بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/rtl-provider)

## BidiText: simplified plain-text isolation

BidiText uses simplified run detection to isolate mixed-direction plain text, such as Latin identifiers, version strings, and dates within Arabic sentences. It leaves the source string unchanged. The browser still performs the actual Unicode bidirectional layout. Do not describe BidiText as a complete Unicode bidi algorithm implementation or as a processor for arbitrary rich HTML.

Props:
- text: string to render. When omitted, a plain-text default slot is used.
- as: wrapper element, default 'span'.
- dir: rtl, ltr, auto, or omitted to use the current scope. auto uses first-strong detection.
- strategy: 'element' by default, or 'chars'.
- enabled: true by default; false renders untouched text.

Both strategies strip pre-existing Unicode bidi control characters from plain-text input before splitting runs (unless enabled is false or the slot contains element markup). The default element strategy wraps runs needing isolation in bdi elements. The chars strategy inserts LRI/RLI and PDI Unicode controls. Prefer elements for normal HTML when copied text should not contain injected control characters.

```vue
<BidiText as="p" dir="rtl" text="الإصدار v1.2.3 متاح الآن" />
<BidiText text="رقم الطلب #4821-B" strategy="chars" />
<BidiText text="آخر تحديث 12-05-2024" :enabled="false" />
```

The default slot can contain text, comments, and fragments. If element markup is present, BidiText preserves that markup unchanged rather than flattening and processing it. Use the text prop when plain-text isolation is required.

Standalone bidi exports:
- classifyChar(char): returns simplified L, R, EN, AN, or N classes.
- detectDirection(text, fallback?): first-strong direction, default fallback ltr.
- hasRtlCharacters(text), isMixedDirection(text): detection helpers.
- stripBidiControls(text): removes Unicode bidi control characters.
- splitBidiRuns(text, baseDir?): returns BidiRun objects with text, dir, isolated, and hasStrong.
- isolate(text, dir?): wraps the whole string in one isolate; default dir is auto.
- isolateRuns(text, baseDir?): isolates runs that need it.
- LRI, RLI, FSI, PDI, LRM, RLM: Unicode control constants.

Sources:
- [BidiText](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/bidi-text)
- [BidiText بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/bidi-text)
- [Bidirectional API](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/api#bidirectional-text)

## Client-side RTL search helpers

Plain `name.includes(query)` fails on Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew text when stored strings contain hamza variants (`أحمد`), harakat (`مُحَمَّدٌ`), tatweel (`عـبـدالله`), Hebrew points (`שָׁלוֹם`), presentation ligatures (`سﻼم`), or local digits (`١٢٣`, `۱۲۳`) while users type bare letters and ASCII digits (`احمد`, `محمد`, `فاطمه`, `مصطفي`, `שלום`, `123`). Pure Vue-free exports from `vue-rtl-kit` handle folding, matching, and UTF-16 highlight offsets:

- foldSearchText(text, options?): string. Applies Unicode NFKC (unfolding presentation forms and lam-alef ligatures), strips Arabic harakat (U+064B to U+065F, U+0670, U+06D6 to U+06ED), tatweel (U+0640), Hebrew points (U+0591 to U+05C7), and Unicode bidi controls, maps U+0622/U+0623/U+0625/U+0671 to U+0627, U+0624 to U+0648, U+0626/U+06CC to U+064A, and U+06A9 to U+0643, lowercases Latin letters, and collapses whitespace runs to a single space ' '.
- matchesSearch(text, query, options?): boolean. Tests whether folded text contains folded query. An empty or marks-only query returns true for any string text; null, undefined, or non-string text (or query) returns false.
- findSearchMatches(text, query, options?): SearchMatch[]. Returns sorted, non-overlapping `{ start, end }` UTF-16 code-unit offsets in the original text. Each `end` offset is extended over trailing combining marks so wrapping slices in `<mark>` never splits a letter from its harakat or niqqud. Preserves exact UTF-16 offsets across surrogate pairs (emoji) and presentation ligatures (`ﻻ`, `ﻷ`). Empty or marks-only queries and null/undefined text return `[]`.

SearchOptions flags all default to true:
- taMarbuta: folds U+0629 (`ة`) to U+0647 (`ه`) when true.
- alefMaqsura: folds U+0649 (`ى`) to U+064A (`ي`) when true (`ئ` U+0626 and Persian `ی` U+06CC always fold to U+064A).
- digits: folds Arabic-Indic (U+0660 to U+0669) and Persian (U+06F0 to U+06F9) digits to ASCII 0-9 when true.

None of the helpers ever throws. Scope is deterministic character folding and exact folded substring matching only — no stemming, root extraction, morphological analysis, or fuzzy matching.

```ts
import { findSearchMatches, foldSearchText, matchesSearch } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

foldSearchText('أَحْمَد عـبـدالله ١٢٣') // 'احمد عبدالله 123'
matchesSearch('فاطمة مصطفى', 'فاطمه مصطفي') // true
matchesSearch('فاطمة', 'فاطمه', { taMarbuta: false }) // false
findSearchMatches('مرحبا مُحَمَّدٌ!', 'محمد') // [{ start: 6, end: 15 }]
```

Sources:
- [Text helpers — Search helpers](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/text-helpers#search-helpers)
- [دوال النص — دوال البحث](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/text-helpers#search-helpers)
- [Search helpers API](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/api#search-helpers)

## v-rtl: element-level direction

v-rtl sets an element's direction; it does not pin the root store. It supports reactive updates, SSR attributes, optional Unicode isolation, and restoration of previous DOM values on unmount.

- Bare v-rtl sets dir="rtl".
- v-rtl:ltr, v-rtl:rtl, and v-rtl:auto take direction from the argument.
- v-rtl.ltr and v-rtl.auto use modifiers when no value or argument is supplied.
- v-rtl.isolate applies RTL plus unicode-bidi: isolate.
- v-rtl="direction" supports reactive rtl/ltr/auto.
- v-rtl="false" means LTR; true, null, and undefined fall back to RTL.
- v-rtl="{ dir: 'ltr', isolate: true }" accepts object configuration.

Arguments and modifiers can be combined, as in v-rtl:ltr.isolate. Import vRtl for local script-setup registration; rtlDirective is its alias. getSSRProps emits dir and the optional isolation style. Unmount restores the previous dir attribute and inline unicode-bidi value.

Sources:
- [v-rtl directive](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/v-rtl)
- [التوجيه v-rtl](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/v-rtl)

## Logical styles in JavaScript

Use native CSS logical properties for normal responsive layout. useLogicalStyles() is for direction-dependent styles and keyboard interactions calculated in JavaScript. It resolves the current scope and returns dir, isRtl, startSide, endSide, sign, toLogical, toPhysical, property, mirror, and arrow.

- toLogical(style, options?): converts physical property names and directional values.
- toPhysical(style, dir?): resolves logical properties using the current scope direction (or an explicit dir override).
- property(name, options?): converts a single property name while preserving casing.
- mirror(value): multiplies an offset by sign, giving 1 in LTR and -1 in RTL.
- arrow(event): maps a KeyboardEvent to 'next' | 'previous' | 'first' | 'last' | 'up' | 'down' | null for the current scope direction (ArrowRight is 'next' in LTR and 'previous' in RTL; Home/End stay 'first'/'last'), returning null when Ctrl, Alt, or Meta is held.
- size option defaults false and enables width/height mappings when true.
- values option defaults true, converting values such as textAlign: 'left' to 'start'.
- shorthands option defaults false and expands 1–4-value physical box shorthands when true.

```ts
import { computed } from 'vue'
import { useLogicalStyles } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

const { arrow, mirror, toLogical, toPhysical } = useLogicalStyles()
const panelStyle = computed(() => toLogical({ marginLeft: '16px', textAlign: 'left' }))
const transform = computed(() => `translateX(${mirror(24)}px)`)
const placement = computed(() => toPhysical({ insetInlineStart: '12px' }))
```

Standalone exports are logicalArrow(key, dir), logicalProperty(property, options?), toLogicalStyle(style, options?), and toPhysicalStyle(style, dir). Physical conversion is useful for rendering paths such as canvas, SVG, email, or legacy consumers that cannot use logical CSS. StyleObject is Record<string, string | number | undefined>, and LogicalArrow is 'next' | 'previous' | 'first' | 'last' | 'up' | 'down'.

## Inline scrolling in LTR and RTL

In modern browsers (Chrome 85+, Firefox, Safari 15.4+), an RTL horizontal scroller starts at scrollLeft === 0 at inline-start (right) and scrolls into negative values toward inline-end (left). Horizontal writing modes (writing-mode: horizontal-tb) only.

Pure Vue-free helpers (direction read from getComputedStyle(el).direction, so dir islands, v-rtl, and RtlProvider work automatically):
- getScrollInline(el): distance from inline-start in px, clamped 0..max, identical in LTR and RTL.
- getScrollInlineMax(el): max(0, scrollWidth - clientWidth).
- scrollToInline(el, offset, options?): clamps offset to 0..max and calls el.scrollTo with the physical left (-clamped in RTL, +clamped in LTR) and optional behavior.
- scrollByInline(el, delta, options?): scrolls by signed inline delta where positive moves toward inline-end.
- scrollInlineEdges(el, tolerance = 1): returns { atStart, atEnd } within tolerance px.

No overflow returns 0 and { atStart: true, atEnd: true }. Null elements, SSR, NaN, and Infinity return 0 or act as a no-op and never throw.

Reactive composable: useInlineScroll(target, options?) returns readonly offset, max, atStart, and atEnd refs plus scrollTo, scrollBy, scrollToStart, and scrollToEnd. It attaches a passive scroll listener and ResizeObserver (when available), re-reads on target and useDirection().dir changes, removes listeners on dispose, and is SSR-safe.

```ts
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { useInlineScroll } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

const track = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null)
const { atStart, atEnd, scrollBy, scrollToEnd } = useInlineScroll(track)
```

Sources:
- [useLogicalStyles](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/use-logical-styles)
- [useLogicalStyles بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/use-logical-styles)
- [Browser support](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/browser-support)
- [دعم المتصفحات](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/browser-support)

## Optional CSS utilities

Import `vue-rtl-kit/styles.css` once. Nuxt loads it by default. Logical layout utilities follow the nearest dir attribute and do not require a stylesheet swap when direction changes.

Design tokens: --rtl-space defaults to 0.25rem, --rtl-border-width to 1px, and --rtl-radius to 0.375rem. Spacing classes multiply --rtl-space.

- ms/me: margin-inline-start/end. Numeric values 0 through 6, then 8, 10, 12; auto is available.
- mi: margin-inline. Values 0 through 4 and auto.
- ps/pe: padding-inline-start/end. Values 0 through 6, then 8, 10, 12.
- pi: padding-inline. Values 0 through 4 and 6.
- text-start, text-end, text-center; float-start/end and clear-start/end.
- justify-start/end and items-start/end for flex alignment.
- start-0/auto, end-0/auto, inset-i-0 for inline positioning. Supply positioning mode and dimensions yourself.
- border-s/e and border-s-0/e-0 for inline borders.
- rounded-s/e and rounded-s-0/e-0 for logical corner radii.
- bidi-isolate sets unicode-bidi: isolate; bidi-plaintext sets plaintext; bidi-nowrap adds nowrap to isolation.
- nums-latn applies lining numerals and Unicode isolation; it does not transliterate digits.
- ltr-only and rtl-only control directional display.
- rtl-flip mirrors directional glyphs; rtl-noflip cancels a flipped ancestor for a nested element.
- rtl-scroll-x sets direction: rtl.

Mirror arrows and chevrons where appropriate, not logos, clocks, checkmarks, or media controls. For run-level isolation inside mixed sentences, use BidiText rather than relying only on a CSS class.

Sources:
- [CSS utilities](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/css-utilities)
- [أدوات CSS](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/css-utilities)

## Locale-aware formatting

useFormat(): ComputedRef<BoundFormatters> binds number, currency, date, list, relative-time, and plural formatters, plus the parseNumber number parser, to the current scope's locale and direction, applying the root instance's configured numberingSystem. The bound formatters follow setLocale(). In templates, use format.formatNumber(...); in script, use format.value.formatNumber(...).

```ts
import { useFormat } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

const format = useFormat()
const amount = format.value.formatCurrency(2500, 'EGP')
const date = format.value.formatDate('2024-05-12', {
  locale: 'ar-EG',
  numberingSystem: 'latn',
  dateStyle: 'long',
  isolate: 'ltr',
})
const reviewers = format.value.formatList(['Ahmed', 'Sara', 'Omar'], { isolate: true })
const edited = format.value.formatRelativeTime(-3, 'day')
const filesLabel = format.value.formatPlural(11, { many: '{count} ملفًا', other: '{count} ملف' }) // '11 ملفًا' when the scope locale is ar
const typed = format.value.parseNumber('١٬٢٣٤٫٥') // 1234.5 when the scope locale is ar-EG
```

Per-call options override bound locale and numbering system. NumberFormatOptions, DateFormatOptions, ListFormatOptions, and RelativeTimeFormatOptions extend the matching Intl options with locale, numberingSystem, and isolate. isolate can be boolean, rtl, ltr, or auto; true uses first-strong detection. This is formatting, not message translation.

Standalone functions:
- formatNumber(value, options?): Intl.NumberFormat.
- formatCurrency(value, currency, options?): ISO 4217 currency formatting.
- formatDate(value, options?): Intl.DateTimeFormat; accepts Date, number, or string; returns an empty string for an invalid date.
- formatList(items, options?): Intl.ListFormat with type ('conjunction', 'disjunction', 'unit') and style. formatList(['Ahmed', 'Sara', 'Omar'], { locale: 'ar' }) gives 'Ahmed وSara وOmar'. With isolate set, every item is wrapped in a first-strong isolate and then the whole result is isolated.
- formatRelativeTime(value, unit, options?): Intl.RelativeTimeFormat with numeric and style; negative values are in the past. formatRelativeTime(-3, 'day', { locale: 'ar-EG' }) gives 'قبل ٣ أيام', and numberingSystem: 'latn' gives 'قبل 3 أيام'. A non-finite value returns an empty string.
- formatPlural(count, forms, options?): picks the CLDR plural form with Intl.PluralRules and replaces every {count} with formatNumber(count, options). forms is Partial<Record<'zero' | 'one' | 'two' | 'few' | 'many' | 'other', string>> with other required; a missing category falls back to other. Arabic uses all six categories (0 zero, 1 one, 2 two, 3-10 few, 11-99 many, 100 other), so n === 1 ? a : b is wrong for Arabic; Hebrew has two, Persian counts 0 as one. options adds type: 'cardinal' | 'ordinal' (English 1st/2nd/3rd) to locale, numberingSystem, and isolate. NaN, Infinity, negative, and fractional counts select the category the rules report without throwing; an empty forms.other or a runtime without Intl.PluralRules returns an empty string; text without {count} is returned as is.
- parseNumber(text, options?): number. The inverse of formatNumber for form input; options are { locale?: string; numberingSystem?: NumberingSystem }, with locale defaulting to 'en'. Number() returns NaN for formatNumber output in ar-EG, fa-IR, he, de, or fr; parseNumber reads it back. It returns NaN for empty or invalid text and never throws.
- transliterateDigits(text, 'latn' | 'arab' | 'arabext'): converts only digits in an existing string.
- withNumberingSystem(locale, numberingSystem?): adds a Unicode -u-nu- locale extension.

NumberingSystem accepts latn, arab, arabext, hanidec, deva, beng, or another runtime-supported string; unrecognized or empty values safely fall back to latn. Actual Intl behavior depends on the runtime's locale support. Each formatter kind (number, date, list, relative time, plural rules) keeps its own bounded LRU cache of 32 Intl instances.

parseNumber rules:
- Separators: the group separator, decimal separator, and minus sign are read from Intl.NumberFormat formatToParts() for the locale and numbering system and cached per locale tag (32 entries). There is no hardcoded separator table. Parse with the same locale and numberingSystem used for formatting; the bound format.value.parseNumber already uses the scope locale and the configured numberingSystem.
- Digits: Western (0-9), Arabic-Indic (U+0660 to U+0669), and Persian (U+06F0 to U+06F9) digits are accepted in every locale, along with the digits of the locale's own numbering system.
- Ignored characters: U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, the isolates U+2066 to U+2069, the no-break space U+00A0, the narrow no-break space U+202F, and ordinary spaces are removed before parsing, so isolate: true output and space-grouped numbers parse. Embeddings and overrides (U+202A to U+202E), tabs, and line breaks are not removed and give NaN.
- Sign: a leading ASCII hyphen, U+2212, or the locale's minus sign negates; a leading plus is allowed.
- Percent: a trailing % or U+066A divides the result by 100 by moving the decimal point exactly, so '5.6%' gives 0.056. A leading percent sign gives NaN.
- Group separators are accepted only between two digits of the integer part, before the decimal separator. Group sizes are not validated, so en-IN lakh grouping ('12,34,567.89') parses, '1,2' is 12 in en, and '1.5' is 15 in de, where '.' is the group separator. Where the locale groups with a space (fr, sv), a space, no-break space, or narrow no-break space between two digits is the group separator and follows the same rule: '1 234,5' parses in fr and '1,2 3' gives NaN, while spaces elsewhere, such as before a percent sign, are still ignored.
- Decimal separator: at most one; '.5' and '5.' are accepted.
- NaN: empty text, letters, currency symbols, compact or exponent notation such as '1e5', a separator the locale does not use, a second decimal separator, a separator on its own, a misplaced sign or percent sign, and non-string input.
- Arabic locales that format with Arabic-Indic digits separate with U+066C and U+066B, so '1,234.5' gives NaN for ar-EG while '1234' parses; use numberingSystem: 'latn' to read Western-style separators.

```ts
import { formatNumber, parseNumber } from 'vue-rtl-kit'

parseNumber('١٬٢٣٤٫٥', { locale: 'ar-EG' }) // 1234.5
parseNumber('۱٬۲۳۴٫۵', { locale: 'fa-IR' }) // 1234.5
parseNumber('1.234,5', { locale: 'de' }) // 1234.5
parseNumber('1 234,5', { locale: 'fr' }) // 1234.5
parseNumber('12,34,567.89', { locale: 'en-IN' }) // 1234567.89
parseNumber('1,234.5', { locale: 'ar-EG', numberingSystem: 'latn' }) // 1234.5
parseNumber('١٢٫٥٪', { locale: 'ar-EG' }) // 0.125
parseNumber('') // NaN
parseNumber('12abc') // NaN
parseNumber('1.2.3') // NaN
parseNumber('1,2 3', { locale: 'fr' }) // NaN
parseNumber(formatNumber(-1234567.89, { locale: 'ar-EG', isolate: true }), { locale: 'ar-EG' }) // -1234567.89
```

Sources:
- [useFormat](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/use-format)
- [useFormat بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/use-format)

## Nuxt 3 and 4 module

Add the module to nuxt.config.ts. Options use the rtl key:

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['vue-rtl-kit/nuxt'],
  rtl: {
    locales: { en: 'ltr', ar: 'rtl' },
    defaultLocale: 'ar',
    numberingSystem: { ar: 'latn' },
  },
})
```

The runtime plugin creates the root store and writes reactive dir and lang attributes through Nuxt head integration into SSR and hydrated markup. No client-only workaround is required. Provide consistent initial locale/direction on server and client.

Nuxt defaults differ from the standalone plugin: locales defaults to { en: 'ltr', ar: 'rtl' } and defaultLocale to en. dir remains optional and, if supplied, pins direction. syncDocument defaults true and htmlClass false. numberingSystem is optional.

Build-time controls:
- autoImports: true by default, importing useDirection, useRtl, useLogicalStyles, useFormat, and useInlineScroll.
- components: true by default, registering RtlProvider and BidiText through Nuxt.
- css: true by default, injecting vue-rtl-kit/styles.css.
- cookie: false by default; a cookie name or { name, maxAge, sameSite } enables persisting the visitor's locale/direction so SSR restores it for returning users. Unknown cookie values are ignored. The browser-only persist and persistKey options of createRtl are excluded from ModuleOptions; in Nuxt, persistence goes through this cookie option so the saved direction is already in the server-rendered HTML.

Important limitations: the runtime plugin is always installed. registerGlobals is forwarded to runtime config; set it to false to disable runtime global registration. components: false disables only Nuxt's build-time component registration; the runtime plugin still globally registers BidiText, RtlProvider, and v-rtl unless registerGlobals is also false. autoImports: false requires explicit composable imports. css: false requires an explicit stylesheet import if you still want the utilities.

Sources:
- [Nuxt module](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/guide/nuxt-module)
- [وحدة Nuxt](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/guide/nuxt-module)

## API entry points and types

Import normal runtime exports and types from vue-rtl-kit. The Nuxt entry point is vue-rtl-kit/nuxt. The CSS entry point is vue-rtl-kit/styles.css. Injection keys rtlInstanceKey and directionScopeKey identify the root instance and nearest scope respectively. isClient tests for both window and document; isServer is its inverse.

Core types:
- Direction = 'rtl' | 'ltr'; DirectionOrAuto additionally allows 'auto'.
- LocaleMap = Record<string, Direction>.
- RtlOptions configures createRtl; ResolvedRtlOptions represents resolved root options.
- DirectionContext describes reactive state and actions; RtlInstance adds root/plugin behavior.
- DirectionState omits isRoot; DirectionStateOptions requires dir and locale and optionally locales and pinned.
- BoundFormatters exposes locale, dir, formatNumber, formatCurrency, formatDate, formatList, formatRelativeTime, formatPlural, and parseNumber.
- PluralForms maps the CLDR plural categories zero, one, two, few, many, and other to message text, with other required; FormatPluralOptions extends FormatOptionsBase with type ('cardinal' | 'ordinal').
- ParseNumberOptions contains optional locale and numberingSystem.
- BidiRun contains text, dir, isolated, and hasStrong.
- LogicalStyleOptions contains optional size, values, and shorthands flags.
- ScrollInlineOptions contains optional behavior; ScrollInlineEdges contains atStart and atEnd; UseInlineScrollOptions contains optional tolerance; UseInlineScrollReturn exposes readonly offset, max, atStart, atEnd plus scrollTo, scrollBy, scrollToStart, and scrollToEnd.
- SearchOptions contains optional taMarbuta, alefMaqsura, and digits booleans (all defaulting to true); SearchMatch contains start and end UTF-16 offsets in the original string.
- RtlDirectiveValue accepts DirectionOrAuto, boolean, undefined, null, or { dir?, isolate? }.

The reference includes signatures for every export and complete type shapes:
- [API reference](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/api)
- [مرجع API بالعربية](https://marwanmaher0.github.io/vue-rtl-kit/ar/api)

## ملخص عربي وحدود الاستخدام

vue-rtl-kit تدير اتجاه الواجهة وتنسيق القيم، ولا تترجم الرسائل ولا تحوّل الواجهة بأكملها تلقائيًا. يدعم الإصدار الموثق Vue 3.3 وما بعده وNuxt 3 و4 على Node 20.11+، ويُثبَّت من npm بالأمر المذكور في قسم التثبيت.

يتبع اتجاه الجذر اللغة حتى يُثبّت عبر dir الأولي أو setDirection() أو toggleDirection(). بعد التثبيت، تغيّر setLocale() اللغة فقط. تقرأ useDirection() أقرب نطاق، أما useRtl() فتصل إلى الجذر المثبّت وترمي خطأ إن لم تكن الإضافة مثبتة. ينشئ RtlProvider نطاقًا محليًا؛ وعند غياب العنصر الحاوي يجب وضع سمات الاتجاه على الأبناء.

BidiText أداة مبسطة لعزل مقاطع النص العادي، وليس محرّكًا للنص الغني ولا تنفيذًا كاملًا لخوارزمية Unicode ثنائية الاتجاه. لا يعالج الوسوم الغنية داخل الخانة؛ استخدم text لعزل النص العادي. يظل المتصفح مسؤولًا عن التخطيط النهائي. تتكيف أدوات CSS المنطقية مع أقرب dir، وتوحّد useInlineScroll ودوال التمرير السطري إحداثيات scrollLeft الأفقي في LTR وRTL لأوضاع الكتابة الأفقية فقط، وتوحّد دوال البحث foldSearchText وmatchesSearch وfindSearchMatches الحركات والهمزات والتطويل ونقاط التشكيل العبرية والأرقام المحلية مع إرجاع نطاقات UTF-16 الأصلية للتظليل دون اشتقاق صرفي أو مطابقة ضبابية، وتنسّق useFormat الأرقام والعملات والتواريخ والقوائم والأزمنة النسبية عبر Intl، وتختار formatPlural صيغة الجمع بفئات CLDR الست للعربية (صفر، مفرد، مثنى، قليل، كثير، غير ذلك) بدل شرط `n === 1` الخاطئ، وتقرأ parseNumber الأعداد المكتوبة بأرقام اللغة وفواصلها وتعيد NaN للنص غير الصالح.

تدعم وحدة Nuxt سمات dir وlang في العرض على الخادم. تعطيل components يوقف تسجيل Nuxt وقت البناء فقط؛ اضبط registerGlobals: false أيضًا لإيقاف التسجيل العام من إضافة التشغيل. راجع الدليل العربي لكل واجهة قبل افتراض سلوك غير موثق.
